blueprint_topic: Management of Care — oncology nurse navigation for barriers, education, and interprofessional coordination
stem: A client with newly diagnosed cancer has missed two appointments because of transportation problems and says, "I do not understand which specialist I am supposed to see next." Which action best reflects the role of the oncology nurse navigator?

options.A: Assess the transportation and understanding barriers, clarify next steps, coordinate with the cancer team, and connect the client with resources that support timely care.
options.B: Clarify the specialist sequence and reschedule visits, but send the transportation concern back to routine scheduling so navigation remains focused on clinical education.
options.C: Address the transportation and education needs now, but defer coordination with the interprofessional cancer team until the diagnostic workup is complete.
options.D: Select the next specialist and treatment sequence independently so missed appointments do not delay care while the oncology team completes its review.

rationale: A is correct. The 2025 joint ONS/AONN+ position statement defines the oncology nurse navigator as an RN with oncology-specific clinical knowledge who offers individualized assistance to help patients and caregivers overcome healthcare-system barriers. It describes comprehensive assessment, education, tailored interventions, decision-support, communication with the interprofessional cancer-care team, provision of education/resources, and facilitation of timely access to health and psychosocial care. The statement also specifies that navigation facilitates transitions through diagnosis and treatment rather than beginning only after treatment starts. B is incorrect because logistical barriers such as transportation are within the barrier-focused navigation role rather than being excluded from it. C is incorrect because interprofessional coordination is a core navigation function and should not be postponed while barriers are already disrupting timely care. D is incorrect because the ONN coordinates and supports care within the interprofessional team rather than independently choosing the client's specialist or cancer-treatment sequence.
educational_objective: Use oncology nurse navigation to assess and address healthcare-system barriers, provide education/resources, and coordinate with the interprofessional cancer team to support informed and timely care without independently selecting the treatment plan.
source_organization: Oncology Nursing Society (ONS); Academy of Oncology Nurse & Patient Navigators (AONN+)
source_document_title: Joint Position Statement: Role of the Oncology Nurse Navigator Throughout the Cancer Trajectory; Oncology Navigation Standards of Professional Practice
source_version_date: Joint ONS/AONN+ position statement approved February 2025 and current ONS page rechecked 2026-08-20; ONS July 7, 2026 navigation update and current 2022 professional standards rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: ONS/AONN+ 2025 Joint Position Statement — opening definition and position bullets: ONN is a professional RN with oncology-specific clinical knowledge who provides individualized assistance to overcome healthcare-system barriers; provides comprehensive assessment, education, tailored interventions and decision support; communicates with the interprofessional cancer-care team; uses the nursing process to provide education/resources that facilitate informed decision-making and timely access to quality health/psychosocial care; navigation facilitates transitions through diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and end-of-life care. ONS 2022 Oncology Navigation Standards — definition of clinical navigator/ONN and oncology navigation: individualized assistance to overcome healthcare-system barriers and facilitate timely access throughout all phases of the cancer continuum. ONS July 7, 2026 update reaffirms the same ONN definition and team-based role.
source_claim_supported: Current ONS/AONN+ guidance directly supports oncology nurse navigation for assessment of healthcare-system barriers, patient education/resources, informed decision support, timely access, and interprofessional coordination across diagnosis and treatment, without assigning independent treatment-selection authority to the navigator.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management, Continuity of Care, Advocacy and Client Education: identify barriers/resources, coordinate referrals and interprofessional services, provide/clarify information, follow unresolved care issues, and support timely continuity of care.
pdf_visual_verification: The ONS/AONN+ evidence relied upon for this item is current HTML; no ONS/AONN+ PDF is relied upon. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care collaboration/referral/case-management content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'oncology nurse navigator transportation barriers appointments education interprofessional timely access diagnosis treatment' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the missed-appointment/navigation construct but removed the uniquely long key and cartoon scope errors. The revised distractors test realistic navigation mistakes: excluding a logistical barrier from navigation, delaying interprofessional coordination until workup completion, and overstepping into independent specialist/treatment selection.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates barrier assessment, education, team coordination, resource linkage, and timely access within the current ONN role.
option_audit.B: Plausible role-silo error; incorrect because transportation is a healthcare-access barrier that navigation is intended to help address.
option_audit.C: Plausible sequencing error; incorrect because coordination with the interprofessional team is a core ONN function and the current barriers are already delaying care.
option_audit.D: Plausible scope-overreach error; incorrect because the navigator coordinates and supports decisions rather than independently selecting specialists or the oncology treatment sequence.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four alternatives contain comparable navigation-process detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel responses to the same access/coordination problem.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after current ONS/AONN+ source-based audit and targeted repository search.
